identity.name: Septinsular Republic
alt_names: Republic of the Seven United Islands

land.text: the seven islands: Corfu, Paxoi, Lefkada, Cephalonia, Ithaca, Zakynthos and Kythira

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: First period of French rule in the Ionian Islands'. After the fall of Venice the islands 'were annexed to the French Republic' (Campo Formio); a joint Russo-Ottoman fleet took them in 1798-1799 and held them until the Republic was set up.

successors.note: Treaty of Tilsit, July 1807: 'the Ionian Islands were ceded once again to Napoleonic France'; infobox 'Ceded to France: 20 August 1807'; infobox 'Succeeded by: Second period of French rule in the Ionian Islands'. British protectorate from 5 November 1815 is a different state (united-states-of-the-ionian-islands).

correction.text: Shape unchanged, but it holds only for 1800 to 20 August 1807 (the Republic's life); for 1807 to 1814 the islands were French again and, from October 1809, British-held in turn

keyframe_review.note: 3,001 km2 for 1800..1814: six cells, the Ionian Islands (5 of the gazetteer region's 7 cells, 1,770 km2 in all) plus a Kythira cell and a Peloponnese edge cell. The page gives no area. The mainland exclaves (Parga, Vonitsa, Preveza, Butrinto) are not in the shape; the treaty left them under the Ottomans ('would remain under Ottoman control'), Ali Pasha seized Butrinto, Preveza and Vonitsa from the French in 1799, and the page leaves Parga unclear. After 1807: 'French troops landed on Corfu on 20 August 1807, and Berthier declared annexation on 1 September 1807'; the British took Zakynthos and Cephalonia on 4 October 1809, Ithaca on 8 October 1809, Kythira on 12 October 1809, Lefkada (surrender 16 April 1810), Paxoi (early 1813), Parga (22 March 1814) and Corfu (June 1814). Those events belong to the French Empire and the British, not to this state.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, but for 1815..1819 it is the United States of the Ionian Islands under British protection (infobox 'British Protectorate: 5 November 1815'), not the Septinsular Republic, which ended in 1807

keyframe_review.note: 3,001 km2, the same six cells. 'The islands were formally organised into the United States of the Ionian Islands under British protection' after the Treaty of Paris (1815). The united-states-of-the-ionian-islands dossier (founded November 1815) carries these years.

region.text: the seven islands: Corfu, Paxoi, Lefkada, Cephalonia, Ithaca, Zakynthos and Kythira

ledger.note: 2 April 1800: the Septinsular Republic is established. Infobox 'Established: 2 April [O.S. 21 March] 1800'; the Treaty of Constantinople between Russia and the Ottomans is dated '6 April [O.S. 25 March] 1800'. Status 'Protectorate of the Russian and the Ottoman Empires'; the Ottomans got suzerainty and an annual tribute of 75,000 piastres. The islands had been taken from the French by a Russo-Ottoman fleet in autumn 1798 and Corfu fell on 4 March 1799 [O.S. 21 February]; the occupying powers handed over the fortresses on 25 August 1801.

20 August 1807: the islands are ceded to France. Infobox 'Ceded to France: 20 August 1807'; 'In the Treaty of Tilsit (July 1807), the Ionian Islands were ceded once again to Napoleonic France'; French troops landed on Corfu on 20 August and Berthier declared annexation on 1 September 1807.

August 1807: the Septinsular Republic ends. The page does not give one end date ('most often placed at 1807, when France annexed it', though the Ionian Senate later argued it had only been suspended); the infobox date of the cession, 20 August 1807, is used.

wars.name: Russo-Ottoman capture of the Ionian Islands

zones.text: the Ionian Islands, taken from the French in autumn 1798 and Corfu on 4 March 1799

wars.outcome: A joint Russo-Ottoman fleet under Admiral Fyodor Ushakov drove the French out of the other islands in autumn 1798 and 'finally captured Corfu on 4 March [O.S. 21 February] 1799'; the Treaty of Constantinople (6 April [O.S. 25 March] 1800) created the Septinsular Republic as a Russo-Ottoman protectorate.
wars.note: Before the state's start; listed because it created the state. No contest event: the state did not exist while the fighting lasted.

certainty.note: Island coasts are sharp by nature; the mainland exclaves (Parga, Vonitsa, Preveza, Butrinto) are not drawn, and the page leaves their status unclear.

notes: Cliopatria's row runs 1800..1819 (two identical 3,001 km2 shapes) but the Republic ended in August 1807 (page: ceded to France 20 August 1807, annexation declared 1 September 1807); 1815..1819 is the British protectorate of the United States of the Ionian Islands (dossier exists, from November 1815), marked wrong here. The years 1807..1815 (second French rule, then British conquests of 1809-1814) are covered by no dossier: the first-french-empire dossier (another part of eu-20) should carry the Ionian Islands from August 1807 and the losses of 4 October 1809 (Zakynthos, Cephalonia), 8 October 1809 (Ithaca), 12 October 1809 (Kythira), 16 April 1810 (Lefkada), early 1813 (Paxoi), 22 March 1814 (Parga) and June 1814 (Corfu), all from this page; the united-states-of-the-ionian-islands note says the same gap exists on its side. The page calls the Republic a 'Protectorate of the Russian and the Ottoman Empires' with Ottoman suzerainty and a tribute of 75,000 piastres: the ottoman-empire (me-10) and russian-empire dossiers should carry vassal_start (April 1800) and vassal_end (August 1807) for septinsular-republic; this dossier cannot, since vassal events belong to the suzerain. The page gives no area; the gazetteer's 'Ionian Islands' region has 7 cells. The end date is disputed on the page (1807 annexation; the Senate's argument of suspension to 1815). The page says the 2nd constitution is 23 November 1803 in the infobox and 5 December 1803 in the text (not territorial). Page budget: 1 page (fetched twice) of 1-2.
